# openinfra_fault_injection (Resource)

A deliberate fault, for resilience testing — the FIS-shaped primitive. Compiles to a Chaos Mesh experiment.

Applying this **breaks things on purpose**. Scope `target` carefully: the blast radius is whatever `label_selector` matches.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Resource name. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `target` (Attributes) The blast radius. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--target))
- `type` (String) `pod-kill`, `pod-failure`, `network-latency`, `network-loss`, `network-partition`, `stress-cpu`, `stress-memory`, `clock-skew`, `io-latency`.

### Optional

- `cpu_load` (Number) Load percent per worker.
- `cpu_workers` (Number)
- `direction` (String) `to`, `from` or `both`.
- `duration` (String) How long the fault lasts. Ignored by `pod-kill`.
- `latency` (String) Delay for `network-latency` / `io-latency`.
- `loss` (String) Packet-loss percent for `network-loss`.
- `memory` (String) Size to consume for `stress-memory`.
- `mode` (String) How many matched pods to hit: `one`, `all` or `fixed-percent`.
- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `partition_peer` (Map of String) `network-partition` only: pod labels the target is cut off from. Omit to isolate it from everything.
- `time_offset` (String) Offset for `clock-skew`, e.g. `+5m` or `-1h`.
- `value` (String) For `mode = fixed-percent`, e.g. `"50"`.
- `volume_path` (String) Mount path to slow for `io-latency`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `namespace/name`, the import identifier.
- `phase` (String)
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether the resource's Ready condition is True. Terraform returns as soon as the object is accepted, so this is usually `false` immediately after apply — the platform reconciles asynchronously.

<a id="nestedatt--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `target`

Required:

- `label_selector` (Map of String) Pod labels to target, e.g. `{ app = "pg" }`.

Optional:

- `namespace` (String) Defaults to the FaultInjection's own namespace.
